question: Assume today is 2026-08-23. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of live births in South Korea in July 2026, as it will be first reported in the national statistics agency's monthly Population Trends release.

target.what: Number of live births occurring in South Korea during July 2026, as first reported in the national statistics agency's monthly Population Trends release (population trend / vital statistics).
target.publisher: Statistics Korea (KOSTAT), via the monthly Population Trends / 인구동향 release
target.cadence: monthly, typically published around the 25th–30th of the second month after the reference month (e.g., July data first reported in late September 2026)
target.caveats: The target period is completed relative to the 2026-08-23 cutoff, but the official July 2026 figure is not yet published and will not be available until roughly late September 2026. The question asks for the number as it will be first reported, so provisional/initial release values are relevant. Liv

candidates.perspective: Statistics Korea monthly vital statistics time series
candidates.hypothesis: The July 2026 live birth count can be projected from the same month in prior years, adjusted for the recent trend and any known shocks. July is typically a high-birth month in South Korea due to seasonality. The most recent published months (e.g., May or June 2026) provide the latest level and trend.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly live births for South Korea for July in each year 2015–2025, and the most recent monthly values published before 2026-08-23 (e.g., January–June 2026 if available). Also useful: year-over-year growth rates for recent months. If the exact July series is unavailable, use the monthly series from KOSTAT's Population Trends or the KOSIS database.
search_hints: Statistics Korea monthly live births July 2025
KOSTAT population trends live births monthly 2026

candidates.perspective: Administrative birth registration data from the Ministry of the Interior and Safety (resident registration)
candidates.hypothesis: Monthly birth registrations reported by the Ministry of the Interior and Safety (MOIS) are highly correlated with KOSTAT live births, though they may differ in timing and coverage. The MOIS monthly resident registration data for July 2026 may be published earlier than KOSTAT's release and can serve as a leading indicator or proxy.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly number of birth registrations (출생신고) in South Korea for July 2026 and recent months, from MOIS resident registration statistics (주민등록 인구통계). Also historical monthly values for July 2023–2025 to establish the ratio between MOIS registrations and KOSTAT live births.
search_hints: MOIS birth registration statistics July 2026 South Korea

candidates.perspective: National Health Insurance Service (NHIS) birth-related claims or health insurance qualification data
candidates.hypothesis: The number of births can be approximated from the number of newborns registered for health insurance or the number of delivery-related medical claims. These administrative data may be available with a shorter lag than KOSTAT and can provide an independent check on the level of births in July 2026.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly counts of health insurance registrations for newborns or delivery-related medical claims in South Korea for July 2026 and recent months. Historical relationship between these counts and KOSTAT live births.
search_hints: NHIS newborn health insurance registration monthly 2026

candidates.perspective: Demographic accounting: births = women of childbearing age × age-specific fertility rates
candidates.hypothesis: The number of live births in July 2026 can be estimated by multiplying the female population aged 15–49 in mid-2026 by the expected general fertility rate or age-specific fertility rates for 2026, then applying a July seasonal factor. This route requires population estimates and fertility assumptions.
candidates.data_to_find: Mid-2026 female population by five-year age groups (15–49) for South Korea, from KOSTAT population projections or resident registration data. Recent total fertility rate (TFR) or age-specific fertility rates (ASFR) for 2025 or 2026, and the historical seasonal index for July births (July births / average monthly births).
search_hints: South Korea monthly birth seasonality July

candidates.perspective: Policy and social shocks affecting births in 2026
candidates.hypothesis: Government policies (e.g., expanded parental leave, baby bonuses), economic conditions, or demographic shocks (e.g., COVID-19 delayed births) may have altered the recent birth trend. Identifying measurable impacts can adjust the projection from historical patterns.
candidates.data_to_find: News or reports on South Korean birth rate trends in 2026, including any policy changes effective in 2025–2026, and monthly birth counts for early 2026 to detect deviations from trend. Also any known one-off events (e.g., changes in registration incentives) that could affect July 2026 registrations.
search_hints: South Korea birth rate 2026 policy impact

candidates.perspective: Published forecasts or projections for South Korea's 2026 births
candidates.hypothesis: Official or private forecasts for 2026 annual births can be combined with the historical July share of annual births to estimate July 2026. Forecasts may incorporate recent trends and policy effects.
candidates.data_to_find: Any published forecast for South Korea's total live births in 2026 (annual) from KOSTAT, research institutes, or international organizations. Also the historical average share of annual births occurring in July (e.g., 2015–2025).

p29.role: January 2026 live births in South Korea (observed level, used as the base for a YoY change factor)

a1.role: ratio of July 2026 births to July 2025 births, applied to the January 2026 level as a proxy for the July 2025 level

methods.rationale: Uses the only observed 2026 birth level (p29, January 2026 = 26,916) as a base and applies a modest positive YoY factor (a1) informed by the +11.7% January change (p30) and the 2025 marriage rebound (p5/p6). The implicit assumption is that the January 2026 level is a reasonable stand-in for the July 2025 level; this is a transfer assumption, not a direct measurement. Shared dependency: both p29 and a1 reflect the same early-2026 upturn, so the method may overstate persistence. Failure mode: if the January 2026 jump was a registration-timing artifact, the July 2026 level could be lower.

a3.role: forecast 2026 annual live births in South Korea

a2.role: July share of annual live births

methods.rationale: Structural route: an annual 2026 birth forecast (a3) times the historical July share of annual births (a2). This is independent of the January 2026 level used in m1 and provides a cross-check. Shared dependency: a3 itself is informed by the same early-2026 evidence as m1, so the two routes are not fully independent. Failure mode: if the annual forecast is wrong or July seasonality shifted, the estimate is biased; the wide ranges on a2 and a3 reflect this.

assumptions.name: July 2026 births relative to July 2025 births
assumptions.rationale: January 2026 births were +11.7% YoY (p29/p30), and the 2025 marriage surge (p5/p6) plus policy support point to continued positive momentum, but monthly birth changes are volatile and the January jump may partly reflect timing; a modest positive factor with wide uncertainty is appropriate.
assumptions.applies_when: Transfers if the early-2026 birth upturn persists through July 2026 and no major shock intervenes between January and July 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that 2026 monthly births turned negative YoY (e.g., a reported decline in spring/summer 2026) or that the January 2026 increase was a one-off registration artifact.

assumptions.name: July share of annual live births in South Korea
assumptions.rationale: July is a near-average month for Korean births; the July share of the annual total has historically been close to 1/12 with mild seasonality. Used only to convert an annual forecast into a July level.
assumptions.applies_when: Transfers if the seasonal distribution of births in 2026 resembles recent years and the annual forecast is for calendar-year 2026 live births.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a large change in the seasonal birth pattern (e.g., a documented shift in conception timing) or a mismatch between the forecast's definition and KOSTAT live births.

assumptions.name: 2026 annual live births in South Korea
assumptions.rationale: 2025 births were roughly 240k; the +11.7% January 2026 jump and the 2025 marriage rebound suggest a modest annual increase, but the level remains far below earlier years. This is a forecast-level input, not the target itself.
assumptions.applies_when: Transfers if the 2026 annual birth total follows the early-2026 momentum and no major demographic or policy shock alters the trajectory.
assumptions.falsified_by: A reported 2026 annual or cumulative birth total outside this range, or evidence that the January 2026 increase reversed.

The best computed estimate for live births occurring in South Korea during July 2026, as it will first be reported by Statistics Korea's monthly Population Trends release, is [[estimate]] persons. The interval is [[p10]] to [[p90]], a model-based [[interval_level]] range conditional on the assumptions, not a demonstrated accuracy guarantee.

The estimate rests on one observed anchor: January 2026 births ([[n_points_kept]] observed point kept). A single assumption, a July 2026-to-July 2025 ratio of [[a1_value]] (range [[a1_low]] to [[a1_high]]), transfers that level forward, informed by the January year-over-year jump and the [n] marriage rebound. The structural cross-check was rejected, so [[n_methods]] method carries [[m1_weight]] weight.

Main risk: the January level may not represent July, and the ratio is assumed, not measured. The July 2026 figure itself, once published, would most improve this.

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 July 2026 births relative to July 2025 births: [[a1_value]] ratio, range [[a1_low]] to [[a1_high]] (range widened by code); used by m1. Overturned by: Evidence that [n] monthly births turned negative YoY (e.g., a reported decline in spring/summer [n]) or that the January 2026 increase was a one-off registration artifact.
final.text:
The best computed estimate for live births occurring in South Korea during July 2026, as it will first be reported by Statistics Korea's monthly Population Trends release, is 28,725 persons. The interval is 19,476 to 42,367, a model-based 80% range conditional on the assumptions, not a demonstrated accuracy guarantee.

The estimate rests on one observed anchor: January 2026 births (6 observed point kept). A single assumption, a July 2026-to-July 2025 ratio of 1.06 (range 0.7539 to 1.508), transfers that level forward, informed by the January year-over-year jump and the [n] marriage rebound. The structural cross-check was rejected, so 1 method carries 100% weight.

Main risk: the January level may not represent July, and the ratio is assumed, not measured. The July 2026 figure itself, once published, would most improve this.

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 July 2026 births relative to July 2025 births: 1.06 ratio, range 0.7539 to 1.508 (range widened by code); used by m1. Overturned by: Evidence that [n] monthly births turned negative YoY (e.g., a reported decline in spring/summer [n]) or that the January 2026 increase was a one-off registration artifact.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

ablation.rule: exclude points from own_history directions and points whose name contains a target entity anchor and whose name or unit shares a stem with the target unit (triangulate/agent/ablation.py)
residual_risks: Own values named by an alias or abbreviation, or with no entity in the point name, are not excluded.

The rule over-excludes on purpose: any point naming the target entity together with the target quantity (for example a survey of the target's visitors) is excluded, even when it is not a value of the target itself.
The model's own memory of the target's history is not removed: it can still shape the plan, the judge's choices and assumption values.
The searcher and the extractor still see pages that contain own values; only the judge's table is filtered.
